kata.name: Wrapper laws above the floor: 7 path equations over adapter/proxy/decorator boundaries and 2 decorator stack orders vs a 13-assertion sampled delegation suite
kata.series_report: No series row: docs/ref/ploeh-grounding.md §6 lists no Adapter/Proxy/Decorator candidate; the kata is HYPOTHESIZED from the ploeh series hub (From design patterns to category theory, 2017-10-04) and pre-registered in fixtures/katas/wrapper-laws/README.md
kata.series_verdict: no prior series run; the pre-registered hypothesis is unique detections against a sampled delegation suite; this entry records the executed comparison and its scope (coverage of unsampled cells, not a new defect class)

expected.detail: the adapter drops the translated auxiliary field on all three rows (the migration lost-cell shape); totality names each dropped cell -> dangling (executed) per row, and the sampled note assertion names row 0 only
the proxy rewires identity at row 1 while the result path still agrees; the proxy identity law (parsed eq 4) fires -> violation (executed)
the reversed decorator stacking order returns a different payload; the stacking law (parsed eq 6) fires at the unsampled stack row -> violation (executed)
a wrapper silently loses an auxiliary cell no law mentions; totality reports it -> dangling (executed), and the field is unsampled

cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/wrapper-laws/faults/03-decorator-order-swaps-result.ct.json --json  # exit 3, 1 finding [violation]

comparison.conventional_baseline: prototype/wrapper_laws_baseline.py --assert: 13 frozen delegation assertions (results for every adapter/proxy/decorator row and one stack order; keys spot-checked one row per wrapper kind; the adapter note spot-checked at row 0; decorator notes and the second stacking order unsampled). Catches 1/4 injected faults, row 0 of W1 only; misses 3/4. A complete 23-assertion cross-product suite would catch all four faults and identify all five unique elements — the result is scoped to the sample.

baseline.artifact: prototype/wrapper_laws_baseline.py sha256:08a61ed2061fc1c962d3b3523abf0fef639d54bffcc263df3c47d7727192772e (13-assertion sampled delegation suite, frozen in fixtures/katas/wrapper-laws/faults.json)

expressibility_gap.invariant: wrapper.call ≡ target.call as a cross-object equation
expressibility_gap.why: catherine equations are parallel paths from one source object (parse/schema.rs::check_equations types both sides against one src/tgt pair); the kata states every law through the wrapper's functional link (`link ∘ target_field = wrapper_field`), which assumes exactly one wrapped target per wrapper. A wrapper delegating to several targets, or a law quantifying over a call argument, has no form

expressibility_gap.invariant: declared optionality (a field that may legitimately be absent)
expressibility_gap.why: every declared arrow is total: an absent cell is a dangling finding. A deliberate absence and a silent loss are the same finding, so W4's 'optional' naming belongs to the library, not the model

expressibility_gap.invariant: runtime dispatch (the wrapper actually calls through)
expressibility_gap.why: the model compares declared result rows; whether the proxy dispatches or fabricates a row is unobservable. L1/L4/L6 are the closest executable statements, not execution traces

expressibility_gap.invariant: object identity (the proxy IS the wrapped entity)
expressibility_gap.why: there is no object-identity or subobject relation in the surface; identity is modelled as agreement of a declared `key` arrow (L2/L5), a weaker claim

discrepancies: Every unique element is a cell the frozen sample skips: two adapter rows' dropped cells, one unsampled proxy identity, one unsampled stack order, one unsampled auxiliary cell. A complete 23-assertion cross-product suite would identify all five, so the positive verdict is scoped to sampled conventional suites; against a dense suite the result is parity (unique 0).

Sample-density sensitivity, stated rather than rounded: results-only sampling (10 assertions) would yield 6 unique elements (all three adapter rows + W2 + W3 + W4); the committed 13-assertion sample yields 5; a complete 23-cell suite yields 0.

The four faults are not equally observable: W2 leaves every result path intact and is invisible to the result-only part of the sample, and W4 is mentioned by no law (totality alone finds it). The unique count is a coverage count, not a defect-class count.
procedure: 1. The laws, fixtures, fault matrix and baseline sample were committed in fixtures/katas/wrapper-laws/ before any run (README.md, faults.json); nothing here is edited after the run.

2. The baseline arm (prototype/wrapper_laws_baseline.py, sha256:1341ad8d6a5f796aacb2d6252170045029b5dedb8a1eb9a7e1e58267ac4dcc18) was executed first over the same fixtures: 13 frozen delegation assertions above the floor (results for every wrapper row, keys spot-checked at one row per wrapper kind, the adapter note spot-checked at row 0, decorator notes and the second stacking order unsampled) and 3 exhaustive assertions at the floor.
3. The probe arm ran the same fixtures through the real binary: `catherine check <fixture> --json`; findings were parsed verbatim (dangling and violation witnesses), never re-derived.

4. Elements were compared, not prose: an element is `dangling:<arrow>#<row>` or `violation:eq<index>@row<row>`; a baseline assertion identifies only the element its pre-registered (wrapper, field, row) cell maps to, and only when it disagrees.
5. Unique detections = probe elements minus baseline-identified elements, per fault; the verdict mirrors harness::derive_probe_verdict (empty unique = killed; unique with an executed arm = survived).
6. Both clean fixtures were re-checked the same way: zero findings and zero baseline detections (a law battery that fires on its own model would invalidate the kata).
7. The unique total and its sample-density sensitivity were recorded as discrepancies, never rounded.
